test_title: PYST 52: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held on 04 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: What is the name of the Comprehensive Household Survey providing labour force statistics in India, which was first conducted in 1955?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Employment-Unemployment Survey (EUS)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Employment-Unemployment Survey (EUS)** is India's most extensive **survey for labor force statistics**, originating in the **9th round of the National Sample Survey (NSS)** in **1955**.
 
• It transitioned to quinquennial surveys, beginning with the **27th round in 1972-73**, following recommendations from the **M. L. Dantwala committee report.**
 
• Over the years, eight quinquennial surveys have been conducted, with the most recent one in 2011-12.
 
• The EUS survey spans an entire year to capture seasonal fluctuations in employment. It assesses economic activity over three reference periods: yearly, weekly, and daily.
 
• These reference periods correspond to three activity statuses: **Usual Status (US), Current Weekly Status (CWS), and Current Daily Status (CDS).**
 
• The Usual Status definition is the broadest measure of employment, while the Daily Status definition is the most conservative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) **is an initiative aimed at gathering comprehensive data on employment and unemployment trends.
 
• **The Quarterly Employment Survey (QES)** forms part of the broader framework known as the All-India Quarterly Establishment-based Employment Survey (AQEES).
 
• **The Area Frame Establishment Survey (AFES)** is a survey method that utilizes a comprehensive sampling frame based on geographical areas to gather data on establishments and businesses for various research and policy purposes.
